exposure: planned mode of delivery in subsequent pregnancy (vaginal vs. cesarean)
delivery characteristics (e.g., induction, prolonged second stage, episiotomy, assisted delivery, birthweight, postterm pregnancy)
outcome: mode of delivery in subsequent delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean)
cohort: 278 women who had experienced an Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injury (OASI) and subsequently delivered again at Tampere University Hospital.
finding: The recurrence rate of OASI was low and the vaginal uncomplicated delivery rate was high among women choosing vaginal delivery after a previous OASI.
mod_finding: After a previous OASI, 78.1% of women planned a vaginal delivery, which was successful in 98.1% of cases with a low rOASI rate of 1.9%, while indications for cesarean delivery were often related to prior OASI characteristics or maternal request/fear of childbirth.
birth_weight: Babies with birthweight > 4,000 g were identified as a characteristic associated with OASI.
gest_age: Babies from postterm pregnancies were identified as a characteristic associated with OASI.
